name: Website
summary: How a whole AhaSlides website page is put together from the DS Marketing sections: every band is a shipped section, the sections keep the spacing and widths they ship with, the page has one H1 and one primary action per section, every content section ends with a call to action and aligns its heading and button by one rule, backgrounds follow the colour rules, imagery is real, the header is the product lockup, and the page is checked at three widths with the DS motion script (staggered reveal, light parallax, count-up numbers). Each rule names the section, token or rule it comes from and the website judge criterion that checks it.
highlights: Every band is a DS Marketing section; a missing one is a DSN ticket, never hand-rolled; Testimonials and FAQ are pasted unchanged
Sections keep their shipped rhythm: 96/64 px padding on desktop, 48/24 at 767 px, 32/16 at 479 px; grids are balanced and layouts vary, at most 3 alternating rows

One H1, one primary action per section, its label written for the page (not always Get started free); every content section closed by a call to action: the hero's primary, except Templates, Integrations, case studies and FAQ, which link to their page; the hero's call to action repeated at the end

Headings centred over symmetric content and left only in a split; checked at 1440, 768 and 375 px with no sideways scroll; motion is staggered reveal, light photo parallax and count-up numbers from one DS script
whenToRead: Read before building, redesigning or reviewing any website page made of full-width sections: a landing, pricing, blog, careers, campaign or help page, on the public site or inside the product.
lead: The Marketing section library gives you the bands; this pattern is how they go together into one page. It adds no new values: every number below is one the shipped sections already use (marketing/*.json), and colour and background come from the colour rules (brand/colour-rules.json, section 3), cited by id and not restated. Typography, UX writing, the page title and favicon, and the logo each keep their own guideline; judge a page on `website` plus `colour`, `background`, `typography` and `ux-writing`.

skillRef.note: The enforceable criteria are anti-slop/criteria.json surfaces.website (W1 to W19). Each rule below names its source (`source`): a Marketing section, a token or a colour rule.

surfaceChoice.useFor: the Navigation section (site header with <aha-product-lockup>), then one Header section: the page's only H1 and its primary call to action, labelled for the page
surfaceChoice.example: Navigation, then a centred Header with a page-specific primary action (Create your quiz free) and Book a demo

surfaceChoice.useFor: Logos directly below the hero (when the page shows customer logos), then Features, Numbers, Testimonials, Pricing and FAQ sections in the order the story needs, each on its own band
surfaceChoice.example: Logos directly below the hero, then Features alternating rows, then Testimonials, then FAQ

surfaceChoice.useFor: the Footer banner, which repeats the hero's primary call to action with the same label, then the Footer
surfaceChoice.example: Footer banner repeating the hero label (Create your quiz free), then the Footer

surfaceChoice.surface: A band the library does not have
surfaceChoice.useFor: a DSN ticket for the missing section; never a hand-rolled band on the page
surfaceChoice.example: A comparison table section: file it, and ship the page without it or with an existing section

the primary and secondary call to action, at the xl height the sections ship

componentBacklog: No missing components. A band the Marketing library does not ship yet is a DSN ticket; add the section there before a page needs it.

rules.rule: Build every band of the page from a DS Marketing section: Navigation, Header, Features, Numbers, Logos, Testimonials, Pricing, FAQ, Footer banner and Footer (Cards inside a section). Paste the section's snippet and change its copy, images and layout choice, never its structure or values. The Logos strip (customer logos, Trusted by) is always the band directly below the hero, never later in the page. A band the library lacks is a DSN ticket, never a hand-rolled section on the page.

Keep the padding each section ships and never override it. Features, Numbers, Pricing and Testimonials ship vertical `--aha-space-96` and side `--aha-space-64` on desktop, `--aha-space-48` / `--aha-space-24` at 767 px and below, `--aha-space-32` / `--aha-space-16` at 479 px and below; Logos and FAQ ship their own (Logos a 32 px vertical, FAQ its own gutter variable). Sections sit flush; add no margin, spacer or divider between them.
source: marketing/testimonials.json — __inner padding and their 767 px and 479 px container rules

rules.rule: Cap section content at 1280 px, centred. Keep a section heading block to 720 px and its lead text to 44ch, as the sections ship them; never stretch body copy across the full width.

Give the page one H1, in the Header section at its display size. Each section has at most one primary button (colour rules 6.1 and 6.2); at most two buttons sit side by side, a primary and a secondary. Write the Sign up or primary call to action label for the page's context, a verb plus what the visitor gets (a template page: Use this template; a quiz-maker page: Create your quiz free; pricing: Start free or the plan name); Get started free is only the fallback when no context-specific label fits. Every content section's call to action is the hero's primary, with the same label, except the Templates, Integrations, case-study and FAQ sections, which link to their own page (rule W18). The closing Footer banner repeats the hero's primary call to action with the same label, not a fixed Get started free.
source: marketing/header.json — the h1 and the primary + ghost pair

rules.rule: Lay out band backgrounds by colour rules 3.2 to 3.5, 3.8 and 3.10: open with a Vivid Pink hero (the Hero Pink header layout, whose Splash hooks are Darker Pink, rule 5.1; the hero is Vivid Pink `#E70E68`, never Darker Pink itself), then alternate full-width white and pale pink bands (a Features section with the `aha-features--accent` class, Vivid Pink at 5%; never an inline `background: var(--aha-bg-accent)` style on the section), starting with white right after the hero, so a full white band always sits between two coloured bands. The band directly after the hero's Logos strip (the customer logos band) is always full white, never the pale pink accent or any other tint. At most two Vivid Pink bands count, the hero being one (a closing Footer banner may be the second, with a white band before it). No black band, no gradient, and no light grey band: light grey belongs to cards inside a section (the Cards gray variant). A white hero is also allowed.
source: marketing/features.json — the section ships a white band; a pale pink band is the `aha-features--accent` class, never an inline `background: var(--aha-bg-accent)` style

rules.rule: Use real `` elements with alt text for pictures: a product screenshot, a committed photo with its licence in the manifest, or the DS placeholder `marketing-assets/image-placeholder.svg` until one exists. Never crop a screenshot. An image fills its container edge to edge at its own ratio (`aha-features__photo--fill`, `aha-marketing-card__media--fill`): no pink frame, no inset. That is the rule for a landscape or square image, alone or among others of the same size. Use the Vivid Pink frame (`aha-features__photo--pink-frame`, `aha-marketing-card__media--pink-frame`: `--aha-vivid-pink-100` with the centre Splash) for any portrait image (taller than wide, ratio under 1), even alone or when every image in the section is the same size, and when a section holds more than one image and those images differ in size or ratio: each sits contained with an even inset, and every frame in the section keeps one ratio (4:3 in a Features row, 3:2 on a card). No stock clip art, emoji used as icons, gradient blobs, glassmorphism or decorative 3D. Icons come from the registry by name with ``.
source: marketing/features.json and marketing/cards.json — the Vivid Pink image frame

rules.rule: Content card links open in a new tab: every Template, Testimonial or case-study, Integration, Article, Feature and Use-case card link, and a Features `Learn more` link, uses `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener"` with a visually-hidden "(opens in a new tab)" inside the link (`aha-marketing-card__visually-hidden`, `aha-testimonials__visually-hidden`, `aha-features__visually-hidden`), so readers keep the page open and stay longer. The section link-out buttons that go to another page (`Browse all templates`, `See all integrations`, `Read customer stories`, `Read the docs`) open in a new tab the same way. In the Footer every link that leaves AhaSlides (the G2 and Training Magazine Network award badges, the DMCA badge, System status and the social channels) opens in a new tab with `rel="noopener"` and a new-tab cue in its label, never some badges in a new tab and others not. Sign up and the hero's primary call to action (Header, Features, Numbers, Pricing, Footer banner), the Navigation links and the Footer links to AhaSlides pages stay in the same tab.
Use the Navigation section for the site header, so the brand is `<aha-product-lockup>`; the app-shell guideline's C1 owns that rule and is not repeated here.

Check the page at 1440, 768 and 375 px: no horizontal scroll at any width, multi-column sections stack to one column, and a stacked image sits on the same side of its text (above or below) in every section of the page. Calls to action keep the xl button height the sections ship; nothing you can tap is smaller than 24 by 24 px.
source: the sections' 991, 767 and 479 px container rules

rules.rule: Motion is staggered reveal, light image parallax and count-up numbers, all from one DS script, and nothing else. Load `lib/marketing-motion.js` once (`<script type="module" src="…/lib/marketing-motion.js">`; on by default, `data-aha-motion="off"` opts a section or the page out). Elements fade in and slide up 24 px as they scroll into view, items that enter together 80 ms apart, timed with `--aha-motion-viz-enter` and `--aha-ease-out`; section photos drift at most 48 px against the scroll; a Numbers value counts up from 0 to its written value once, when it is half in view. Hover transitions use `--aha-motion-*` and `--aha-ease-*`. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` nothing moves and every final value shows at once. No scroll-jacking, no autoplaying carousel or video, no hand-written scroll or parallax script on the page; the Logos strip's shipped loop, which stops under reduced motion, is the one continuous motion allowed.
source: lib/marketing-motion.js — reveal, stagger, parallax and count-up
marketing/features.json — the video variant never autoplays
marketing/logos.json — the loop and its reduced-motion stop

rules.rule: Decide each section as text-led or image-led from its job. Image-led means readers compare the pictures (themes, slide types): use the Cards `aha-marketing-cards__grid--image-led` layout, at most 2 columns on desktop so every image is at least half the content width, 4 items as 2 by 2, an odd count with the first item as a wide feature card (image two thirds, title beside it), and 1 column below 768 px. Templates are the exception: a grid of Template cards is always 3 columns at 992 px and wider (`aha-marketing-cards__grid--templates`), n full rows of 3 and so a multiple of 3 templates, never the 2-column image-led layout and never W11 balancing (no 2 by 2 for four, no centred lone card); tablet and phone stay as Cards ships them. Text-led means the words carry it (steps, benefits, use cases) and follows W11 for its column count. Cards inside a section are transparent and add no padding or max-width of their own.
source: marketing/cards.json — the image-led grid and the transparent cards band
marketing/features.json — `.aha-features .aha-marketing-cards__grid` drops the grid's padding and cap

rules.rule: Balanced grids: a card or feature grid (not templates, which are always 3 by n on desktop, W10) never leaves an empty column slot or sits off-centre. The column count follows the item count: 1 item is one centred column, 2 items are 2 columns, 3 are 3, 4 are 2 by 2, and 5 or more are 3 columns with a short last row centred. The Cards grid, the Features icon grid and the Numbers stats do this by default at 992 px and wider, and centre a lone last card at 768 to 991 px; never override `grid-template-columns` to leave a gap.
source: marketing/features.json — the balanced Features icon grid

rules.rule: No layout fatigue: a section shows at most 3 alternating image/text rows, and two alternating-row sections never sit back to back (a fourth row or a second alternating section becomes Cards, an icon grid or Tabs). Numbered steps use the Steps row (Cards `aha-marketing-cards__grid--row`), never alternating rows. Consecutive sections change layout: no two neighbouring sections share the same layout.
source: marketing/features.json — the alternating, icon grid and Tabs layouts

rules.rule: Testimonials and FAQ use the current DS sections verbatim: paste a Testimonials layout (Simple left aligned, Case study cards or Quote cards) and the FAQ section (marketing/faq.json) with their markup and CSS unchanged, changing only copy and images. Never a hand-built, older or look-alike copy (`aha-testimonials--centered-01`, an FAQ without `aha-faq__trigger` buttons with `aria-expanded` and the plus/minus icon, a hand-made accordion).

One type ramp per page: every text role uses exactly one DS type token across all Marketing sections on the page, so the same role has the same size, weight and family everywhere. Section heading (h2): `--aha-size-h2` 40 px, 32 px at 991 px and below, 24 px at 479 px and below, semibold, line-height `--aha-line-height-heading`. Section lead and quote text: `clamp(--aha-size-l, 1.4vw, --aha-size-xl)` 16 to 20 px, regular. Alternating row title: `--aha-size-h4` 24 px, 20 px at 479 px and below, semibold. Item or card title in any component (Cards, Features, Steps, image-led cards, Numbers stat title, Pricing benefit, FAQ question): `--aha-size-xl` 20 px, semibold. Body: `--aha-size-l` 16 px, regular. Meta or caption: `--aha-size-default` 14 px, regular. Eyebrow: `--aha-size-sm` 12 px, semibold, uppercase. Stat number: `clamp(--aha-size-h2, 5vw, --aha-size-h1)` 40 to 48 px, semibold. Every heading and number is Plus Jakarta Sans, the section's own `--aha-font-product`: never `--aha-font-display` (Nunito) or a page or Webflow font. The shipped sections already resolve to this ramp, so paste them unchanged and never restyle a text role on the page.
source: marketing/cards.json, features.json, numbers.json, pricing.json, testimonials.json, faq.json, footer-banner.json, header.json — the shared type tokens

rules.rule: Heading alignment is one rule for the whole page. A section heading block (eyebrow, h2, lead) is centred whenever it sits full width above the content: Features, Numbers, Pricing, Testimonials quote cards, Cards and FAQ in their symmetric layouts, with the `--center` header class or the section's own centring (the FAQ title centres itself with `text-align:center`, so a page or Webflow reset cannot pull it left). It is left aligned only where it shares a row or column with the content: the Features `icon-cards-side-header`, the Numbers `actions-icons` and `split-image*`, the Pricing `featured-cards-*` and the Testimonials `simple-left-aligned` and `case-study-cards` (arrows on the same row) layouts. Never a centred heading over a left-pinned body or the reverse, and never one section on the page centred while a symmetric neighbour is left aligned.

Every content section after the hero ends with one call to action, so the reader is never left at a dead end: the button row shipped in the section (`aha-features__cta`, `aha-numbers__cta`, `aha-testimonials__cta`, `aha-faq__cta`, or the section's `__actions` in a split header). Exempt: the Logos strip (it sits under the hero, which has the call to action), Pricing (the plan buttons are its call to action), the Footer banner (it is the primary call to action) and Navigation and Footer. The call to action follows its heading block: centred under the content when the heading is centred, left under the content (or inside the left header) when the heading is left aligned. In a split layout, a text column beside a media column (Features `icon-list-photo`, `tabs-screenshots` and an `alternating-screenshots` section with a single row, Testimonials `simple-left-aligned`), the button row sits inside the text column under the text, left aligned with it (`aha-features__cta--start` in `aha-features__column`, or the row's own `aha-features__actions` for the single alternating row, with no second button row under the section), even when the eyebrow and heading above are centred: never centred under the whole row. Never a lone left button under a centred or symmetric grid, never a centred button under a left aligned section, never a button page-built beside the shipped one. Sign up and the hero's primary call to action stay in the same tab (W15). Only four kinds of section send the reader to another page, and only when the page has them: Templates go to the template library (`Browse all templates`), Integrations to the integrations page (`See all integrations`), case studies, testimonials included, to the case studies (`Read customer stories`), and the FAQ to the AhaSlides docs (`Read the docs`); these are secondary buttons whose label names the destination, never a bare `View more`, `Learn more` or `Click here`; these four link-outs open in a new tab (W15). Every other content section, Features, Numbers, how-it-works steps and use cases among them, ends with the hero's primary call to action: the shipped button turned primary (drop the `--ghost` or `--secondary` modifier), with the hero's own label and link, the page-specific label W4 asks for (Sign up in the snippets is only the example). Never the hero's primary call to action on a Templates, Integrations, case-study or FAQ section, never a link to another page from any other section.
source: marketing/features.json, numbers.json, testimonials.json, faq.json — the __cta rows

rules.rule: A testimonial author block is one left aligned unit: avatar, name and role sit in one row, the name and role text stacked and left aligned, and the quote above it is left aligned too, even inside a centred section. In a row of quote cards the quote text takes the top track and the author row the bottom track of the same grid (CSS subgrid), so every author row sits on one baseline however long the quotes are. Never a centred name or role under a left aligned quote, an avatar floating on its own line, or author rows at different heights across cards. A Testimonials section shows at most three testimonial or case cards, and the quotes in a row are of similar length: the longest within about 1.5 times the characters of the shortest and none over 160 characters, so there is never one long quote beside short ones.
source: marketing/testimonials.json — person, person-text, quote and the quote-cards subgrid

reuseNote: Doc-only pattern: the DS ships the sections, not a page wrapper. A page is the sections' snippets pasted in order on one page that loads variables.css once; this pattern is the conventions plus the binary criteria (anti-slop/criteria.json, surfaces.website) a builder self-judges against.

selfCheck.label: every band is a DS Marketing section, none hand-rolled
sections keep their shipped padding at each width, with nothing between them
content capped at 1280 px; heading block 720 px; lead text 44ch
one H1; one primary button per section; at most two buttons side by side; hero CTA repeated at the end; label written for the page
band backgrounds follow colour rules 3.2 to 3.5, 3.8 and 3.10; pink hero, white and pale pink body, no grey band
real images with alt text or the DS placeholder; registry icons; no clip art, emoji icons, blobs or glass
the site header is the Navigation section with <aha-product-lockup>
no horizontal scroll at 1440, 768 and 375 px; consistent stacking; targets at least 24 px
motion is the DS script only: staggered reveal, light photo parallax, numbers count up from 0, all off under reduced motion; no scroll-jacking or autoplay
in an image-led section, every image is at least half the content width and uncropped
card and feature grids have no empty slot and are centred; column count follows the item count
at most 3 alternating rows in a section, never two alternating sections in a row, steps use the Steps row, neighbouring sections change layout
Testimonials and FAQ are the current DS sections, pasted unchanged
one type ramp: each text role (h2, lead, item title, body, quote, meta, stat) has one size, weight and family on the whole page; all Plus Jakarta Sans
content card links open in a new tab with rel noopener and hidden new-tab text; Sign up and navigation links stay in the same tab
section headings centred when full width over the content, left only when they share a row or column with it; FAQ title centred

every content section ends with one call to action aligned like its heading: the hero's primary with its label, except Templates, Integrations, case studies and FAQ, which link to their page named in the label; Logos, Pricing and the Footer banner exempt
testimonial avatar, name, role and quote left aligned; author rows on one baseline across cards
